boundaries: Original production controls establish stale status, presentation, export, range, clock and exact integer defects. Draft controls and later newly discovered custom metadata/integer findings are separately archived.

All browser tests use actual embedded functions and finite offline stubs; six Chrome component cases cover original/final layout, native keys, reduced motion and exact JSON source parsing. No application network or production data was used.

Ordinary unsafe integer tokens become browser-local decimal strings; server JSON-number types are unchanged. Legacy browsers without source context explicitly reject potentially unsafe integer-valued results, including ambiguous large whole-valued floats.

Status receipt age does not guarantee CPU/disk sample age. Cache refresh remains background and can exceed its sixty-second TTL. No index-readiness-category UI or new coverage guarantee is introduced.
One timed browser status owner has no effect on ingestion/query cancellation ownership, server task quotas or storage write barriers. There is no performance benchmark claim.
Existing Chart.js4.5.0 bytes match the published package and carry verified SHA384 plus anonymous CORS; downloaded code was not executed during verification.
Linux/macOS CI select Node24 through a pinned official action. The Rust toolchain, Cargo dependencies and data formats are unchanged.
Gossip/query resource policy, verified repair and integrated offline acceptance remain open. Live sync and staging acceptance follow offline completion; this is not release readiness.
